queries.query: the seeress recalling the age of Ymir, before sand or sea or sky existed, when there was only a great emptiness and no green thing
queries.note: 'Yawning gap', 'cool waves', 'earth had not been nor heaven above' paraphrased; Ymir kept as a name any reader knows.

queries.query: the prophecy that the sun goes dark, the land sinks under the ocean and flame reaches heaven itself, before a green earth rises from the waves once more
queries.note: 'Hot stars down from heaven are whirled', 'life-feeding flame', 'cataracts fall' paraphrased; the prophecy framing kept — the poem is the wise-woman's prophecy.

queries.query: after the destruction of the world, does it return renewed
queries.note: World-renewal after cataclysm is answered across traditions. No target — graded post-hoc.
